react_result.final_narrative_text: Four pathway-analysis tools (RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog m/z-network analysis, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant biological signature. RaMP reports KEGG:map00052 and SMPDB:SMP00043 (FDR 8.76×10⁻¹⁵, fold enrichment ~1450), with five input metabolites (myo-inositol, sucrose, galactitol, glycerol, galactinol) mapping to 30–31 pathway members. The same pathway is ranked #4 by mummichog on the human metabolic network (p=0.0058, 11/12 compounds overlapped) and is the single top hit in MetaboAnalystR (p=5.65×10⁻⁹). Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) shares the identical driver set and is equally significant, reflecting that the Leloir pathway perturbation underlies the classic disease phenotype. Secondary signals appear in glycerophospholipid metabolism (RaMP: REACT:R-HSA-1483257, FDR 5.24×10⁻⁴; mummichog: rank 6, p=0.011) driven by myo-inositol and glycerol, and in small-molecule transport (RaMP: REACT:R-HSA-382551, FDR 5.39×10⁻⁵) where aspirin (acetylsalicylate) appears alongside myo-inositol and glycerol. Aspirin additionally maps to WP:WP4707 'Aspirin and miRNAs' (FDR 7.85×10⁻⁴). The five core galactose-cluster metabolites collectively account for 6 of the 9 input compounds; the remaining three (methionine sulfoxide, D-glucose, allysine) do not reach significance in any single pathway but D-glucose appears broadly in mummichog's hexose-metabolism network module.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis tools converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant signal. RaMP ORA reports Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and its disease counterpart Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) at FDR 8.76×10⁻¹⁵, both with 5 of 9 input metabolites overlapping the pathway roster. The KEGG namespace (KEGG:map00052) confirms the same pathway with identical statistics. Mummichog independently recovers galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at p=0.0086 and starch and sucrose metabolism (MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism) at p=0.0094, the latter capturing sucrose as a direct disaccharide input. The five driver metabolites are myo-inositol (C00137), sucrose (C00089), galactitol (C01697), glycerol (C00116), and galactinol (C01235); D-glucose, methionine sulfoxide, allysine, and aspirin are not members of the KEGG map00052 compound roster and do not contribute to the primary enrichment signal. Aspirin (KEGG:C01405) does appear in Transport of small molecules (REACT:R-HSA-382551, FDR 5.39×10⁻⁵) alongside myo-inositol and glycerol, identifying a secondary but significant pathway hit. Glycerol additionally maps to the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, FDR 2.02×10⁻⁴) via RaMP.

RaMP ORA reports Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and its disease counterpart Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) at FDR 8.76×10⁻¹⁵, both with 5 of 9 input metabolites overlapping the pathway roster. The KEGG namespace (KEGG:map00052) confirms the same pathway with identical statistics. Mummichog independently recovers galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at p=0.0086 and starch and sucrose metabolism (MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism) at p=0.0094, the latter capturing sucrose as a direct disaccharide input. The five driver metabolites are myo-inositol (C00137), sucrose (C00089), galactitol (C01697), glycerol (C00116), and galactinol (C01235); D-glucose, methionine sulfoxide, allysine, and aspirin are not members of the KEGG map00052 compound roster and do not contribute to the primary enrichment signal. Aspirin (KEGG:C01405) does appear in Transport of small molecules (REACT:R-HSA-382551, FDR 5.39×10⁻⁵) alongside myo-inositol and glycerol, identifying a secondary but significant pathway hit. Glycerol additionally maps to the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, FDR 2.02×10⁻⁴) via RaMP.
